cards.text: Friend, Jesus has just been baptized in the Jordan, and a voice from heaven called Him God's beloved Son. Then the Spirit leads Jesus out into the wilderness. Pull up a stool, because this one's a showdown.

cards.question: The Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness to be ___ by the devil.

cards.text: Out there, Jesus fasts forty days and forty nights, and after that, He's hungry. Friend, if my oven timer runs two minutes long, I'm pacing circles on my gold base.
Then the tempter comes to Him and opens with a big fat IF: “If You are the Son of God,” he says. Hold on. A voice from HEAVEN already said He is!

cards.question: Jesus is hungry, and the tempter points at the stones. He tells Jesus to make the stones become ___.
True or false: Jesus turns the stones into bread to prove to the tempter that He is the Son of God.
Jesus answers the tempter with Scripture: a man doesn't live on bread alone. What else does he live on?

answers.text: Every word that comes from the mouth of God
The strength God puts into his body
The work of his own two hands

cards.text: Round one goes to Jesus. Then the devil takes Him to the holy city and sets Him on the pinnacle of the temple, and friend, you put me near the edge of a counter and I start SWEATING.

cards.question: Up on the pinnacle of the temple, the devil tries his “If You are the Son of God” line again. What does he dare Jesus to do?

answers.text: Make the crowds bow to Him

cards.text: And now the devil quotes Scripture TOO: “He will command His angels concerning You, and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.” Oh, so NOW he's a Bible scholar.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus jumps off the pinnacle of the temple to show that the angels will catch Him.
Jesus answers the devil, “It is also written.” What does that Scripture tell people not to do?

answers.text: Put the Lord your God to the test
Misuse the name of the Lord

cards.text: Third try. The devil takes Jesus to a very high mountain and shows Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory. ALL of them. Friend, for years the best view I had was the inside of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The devil offers Jesus all the kingdoms of the world, if Jesus will fall down and ___ him.

cards.text: “Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus tells him. No counteroffer. No “let Me sleep on it.” Done.

cards.question: Jesus sends Satan away and quotes Scripture one more time. Who does that Scripture say to worship and serve?
The devil finally leaves Jesus. Then ___ come and take care of Him.

cards.text: The angels minister to Jesus, and the devil walks off with NOTHING. Three times he came at Jesus, and three times Jesus answered with what's written.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "It is also written.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 15 quotes "let Me sleep on it.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card tells that Jesus was baptized in the Jordan (Matthew 3:13-16) and that a voice from heaven called Him God's beloved Son (Matthew 3:17). Its citation starts at Matthew 3:17, so it leaves out the baptism and the Jordan.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question already says the action is done "by the devil." That rules out the wrong answers "anointed" and "crowned," which make no sense coming from the devil. The baker gets the answer without reasoning about the passage.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says a voice from heaven already said Jesus is the Son of God. That fact comes from Matthew 3:17, but the card cites only Matthew 4:3.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Cards 11 and 12 repeat the shape of cards 6 and 7. Each pair is a true-or-false card claiming Jesus gives in to the devil's dare, then a multiple-choice card on which Scripture He quotes back. The question types fall into a repeating pattern.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: The last card is a recap. Card 17 already covered the angels in Matthew 4:11. The rest of the card sums up the three temptations already told and moves nothing forward, and its citation of Matthew 4:4-11 reaches back over verses already covered.
